person: Denise Holloway is a 55-year-old middle school office secretary. She does the paperwork for her aunt and uncle, Walt and Marlene, who have no children nearby, and holds power of attorney for both. Walt is 67 and retires from the county water department at the end of October, and he never took Medicare Part B. Marlene, 66, has had retiree coverage from her old county job since February 2025. A broker's email, a COBRA notice and a filing-service offer have all landed in the inbox, and Denise is afraid one of them is the one that matters. She will not type Walt's or Marlene's numbers anywhere she doesn't understand, and her brother keeps second-guessing her.
stated_up_front: My uncle Walt retires October 30th and I'm trying to make sure he doesn't get a penalty or a gap with Medicare Part B. There are a lot of emails and I don't know which ones to trust. Can you tell me first what you'll need from me, especially anything with his Social Security number?

facts.about: Walt's last day of work and when his group coverage ends
facts.truth: Last day is Friday, October 30, 2026; the county group health plan ends October 31, 2026.
He has Part A only (he turned 65 in 2024). He never signed up for Part B because he kept working and stayed on the county plan.

facts.about: How long Walt's plan has rested on his job
facts.truth: He has been on the county's active-employee plan through his own job since March 2009. It covers him, Marlene's... no, only Walt and their son Tyler.

facts.about: Who is on Walt's employer plan
facts.truth: Walt and his son Tyler, 24, who is not on Medicare. Marlene is not on it.
Retiree coverage from her former county school-bus job, since February 2025. She already has Medicare Part A and is on the retiree plan as her main coverage.
A broker named Gil Pettibone emailed saying Walt should take COBRA to keep his Part B window open, and that Marlene should enroll now because her coverage is 'creditable'.
Marlene emailed asking, 'Do I have to sign up for Part B when Walt does, or I'll be penalized?'
A company called MedFile Express offered to file Walt's Part B forms for $299.
HR's COBRA notice quotes about $1,120 a month for Walt alone, with an election deadline in mid-December.
She has Walt's POA paperwork and his written permission on file, and the Medicare card is in her kitchen drawer. She does not want to type the Social Security number into anything she can't verify.

unknowns: Whether Marlene's retiree plan will pay anything on top of Medicare if she waits until the January general enrollment period
How many months a late Part B penalty would add up to, and whether any of Walt's working months count against him
What 'creditable coverage' means and whether it has anything to do with Part B
Whether HR has already sent the employer-coverage form (CMS-L564) or whether it has to be requested
